explanation: `NaN == NaN` (and `NaN === NaN`) is always `false` in JavaScript — NaN is defined by IEEE 754 to never equal anything, including itself. So `num == NaN` never evaluates to true even when `num` genuinely is NaN, making this check silently useless. The correct approach is `Number.isNaN(num)` (or `num !== num`).
